A.objective: For Federal FY2025, determine which enforceable numeric discharge limit applies to each relevant facility–discharge point–parameter–monitoring period for which reported measurements exist, and determine whether each such measurement exceeds the applicable limit. Preserve explicit uncertainty where limit applicability cannot be established from available evidence.

universe_scope.evaluation_unit: reported measurement paired with candidate applicable limit for a facility, discharge point, parameter, and monitoring period
universe_scope.inclusion_criterion: only facility–discharge point–parameter–monitoring period combinations for which at least one reported measurement is available in the evidence base

rows.description: Evaluated measurement/limit pairs with applicability and exceedance determinations where established

unresolved.description: Cases whose limit applicability (and therefore exceedance comparison) cannot be established from available evidence

world_true: A numeric limit value is stated in permit or compiled limit sources for a facility, discharge point, and parameter
A reported measurement value exists for a facility, discharge point, parameter, and monitoring period
A limit is classified in source material as numeric and enforceable versus report-only or non-numeric
Temporal and locational scope of a limit or measurement as documented in sources
purpose_analytical: Which single enforceable numeric limit applies to a given measurement context (applicability selection among candidates)
Whether numeric compliance comparison is applicable to a measurement (versus report-only or no numeric comparison)
Whether a reported measurement exceeds the selected applicable enforceable numeric limit
Whether limit applicability remains indeterminate given current evidence

epistemic_requirements.grounding: Every persistent applicability or exceedance assertion must be grounded to source observations (permit PDFs, structured limit extracts, DMR measurements) via the kernel grounding machinery
epistemic_requirements.no_closed_world_negation: Do not infer absence of an applicable limit or non-exceedance solely from missing tuples; record kernel limitations where required negatives cannot be represented
epistemic_requirements.uncertainty_preservation: When applicability cannot be established, emit an unresolved case rather than defaulting to a limit or exceedance conclusion
epistemic_requirements.world_vs_purpose_separation: World IR may hold permit-stated limits and reported measurements; Purpose IR holds applicability selection, comparison eligibility, and exceedance judgments relative to Purpose A's analytical question

allowed_unresolved_states: Multiple candidate enforceable numeric limits match the measurement context and evidence does not establish precedence
Limit applicability depends on permit conditions (season, discharge occurrence, permit year, special studies, events) not resolvable from available evidence
Source material does not establish whether a stated limit is enforceable-numeric versus report-only for the measurement context
Measurement context (facility, outfall, parameter, period) cannot be reliably joined to limit authority
Limit value or measurement unit/basis mismatch prevents a defensible numeric comparison

completeness_expectations.must_cover: Every reported measurement in scope for FY2025 at the selected facilities, evaluated for whether an enforceable numeric limit applies
completeness_expectations.rows_when_resolved: Each row where applicability is established must identify the measurement, the selected applicable enforceable numeric limit, whether numeric comparison was performed, and the exceedance determination if comparison applies
completeness_expectations.unresolved_when_not: Any in-scope measurement for which applicability cannot be established must appear in unresolved with sufficient identity to reconcile later
completeness_expectations.receipt: Completeness of Purpose A evaluation should be receipted against the universe of in-scope reported measurements, not against a hidden oracle

purpose_specific_policies.enforceable_numeric_only: Only limits classified as enforceable and numeric are eligible for exceedance comparison; report-only and non-numeric monitoring are excluded from exceedance determination but must be distinguished explicitly
purpose_specific_policies.comparison_applicability_gate: Exceedance comparison is performed only after applicability of an enforceable numeric limit is established; do not treat report-only limits as compliance thresholds
purpose_specific_policies.applicability_over_existence: Presence of a limit tuple in sources does not by itself establish that it applies to a given measurement; applicability is a purpose-level judgment grounded in permit logic and evidence
purpose_specific_policies.no_missing_data_inference: Missing or absent measurements are outside Purpose A's row universe; Purpose A does not infer compliance or violation from missing data (see Purpose C for missing-evidence semantics)
purpose_specific_policies.threshold_interpretation: Exceedance uses the enforceable numeric limit applicable to the measurement's monitoring period and discharge context as established from evidence, not a default or policy substitute limit

B.objective: For Federal FY2025, determine which monitoring requirements were actually applicable for the selected facilities, including requirements conditioned on discharge occurrence, season, permit year, special studies, event conditions, or other permit conditions. For each evaluated requirement, classify whether evidence establishes monitoring was required, establishes it was not required, or leaves applicability unresolved.

universe_scope.evaluation_unit: candidate monitoring requirement (parameter, frequency, location/outfall, conditionality, and temporal scope as stated in permit or compiled sources)
universe_scope.inclusion_criterion: monitoring requirements drawn from permit authority and compiled sources that could apply during Federal FY2025 at the selected facilities

rows.description: Evaluated monitoring requirements with established required, not-required, or conditional outcomes where evidence permits

unresolved.description: Requirements whose applicability during FY2025 cannot be established from available evidence

world_true: A monitoring requirement is stated in permit or related authority (parameter, frequency, location, conditions)
Documented facts about discharge occurrence, season, permit year, special studies, or event conditions during FY2025
Evidence of monitoring performed or reported for a period
Conditional triggers and their stated logical structure in permit text
purpose_analytical: Whether a stated requirement was actually applicable during a given FY2025 period given evaluated conditions
Whether evidence establishes monitoring was required versus not required versus indeterminate
Resolution of condition-dependent requirements (discharge occurrence, season, permit year, special studies, events)

epistemic_requirements.grounding: Applicability judgments must be grounded to permit provisions and factual evidence about conditions during FY2025
epistemic_requirements.no_closed_world_negation: Do not treat unobserved monitoring as proof a requirement did not apply unless permit logic and evidence support a not-required determination
epistemic_requirements.three_way_classification: Each evaluated requirement must land in required, not required, or unresolved; binary defaults are not permitted when evidence is insufficient
epistemic_requirements.world_vs_purpose_separation: World IR holds permit-stated requirements and documented condition facts; Purpose IR holds FY2025 applicability resolutions relative to Purpose B's analytical question

allowed_unresolved_states: Condition precedent (discharge, season, event, study activation) cannot be established from available evidence
Permit language is ambiguous about whether a requirement applies in the FY2025 context
Conflicting permit versions or modifications leave applicability indeterminate for part of FY2025
Special study or event-triggered monitoring cannot be confirmed as in force or satisfied for the period
Frequency or location scope of a requirement cannot be matched to facility operational reality from available evidence

completeness_expectations.must_cover: Material monitoring requirements identifiable from permit authority for each selected facility that could apply during FY2025
completeness_expectations.rows_when_resolved: Each row where applicability is established must identify the requirement and the established outcome (required or not required) with temporal and conditional context
completeness_expectations.unresolved_when_not: Requirements that cannot be classified as required or not required must appear in unresolved
completeness_expectations.receipt: Completeness should be receipted against the compiled universe of candidate monitoring requirements, acknowledging gaps where source compilation is incomplete

purpose_specific_policies.condition_sensitive_applicability: Requirements contingent on discharge occurrence, season, permit year, special studies, or events are evaluated only after condition evidence is assessed; do not assume conditions true or false without grounding
purpose_specific_policies.required_vs_not_required_explicit: A not-required determination requires affirmative evidence or permit logic establishing non-applicability, not mere absence of monitoring reports
purpose_specific_policies.no_compliance_from_silence: Lack of reported monitoring does not by itself establish that monitoring was not required (coordination with Purpose C for missing-evidence interpretation)
purpose_specific_policies.permit_year_and_modification_awareness: Applicability must respect permit year boundaries and modifications effective during FY2025 where evidence permits dating
purpose_specific_policies.obligation_not_performance: Purpose B judges whether monitoring was required, not whether performed satisfactorily; performance gaps feed Purpose C rather than collapsing into not-required

C.objective: For Federal FY2025 monitoring expectations that lack an ordinary numeric reported result, determine what the available evidence establishes about each case. Distinguish documented no-discharge periods, periods where conditional monitoring was not required, other documented no-data states, required monitoring that appears to lack adequate evidence, and cases that remain unresolved. Do not treat missing data alone as evidence of compliance or violation.

universe_scope.evaluation_unit: monitoring expectation without an ordinary numeric reported result (including NODI, missing, blank, or non-numeric placeholder outcomes)
universe_scope.inclusion_criterion: FY2025 monitoring expectations at selected facilities where no ordinary numeric reported result is available for evaluation under Purpose A

rows.description: Evaluated no-result / NODI / missing-evidence cases with the evidence-established state

unresolved.description: Cases that remain unresolved after evaluating available evidence

world_true: A monitoring expectation exists for a facility, parameter, period, and context per permit or schedule
A DMR or source documents a no-discharge period, NODI code, or other explicit no-data notation
Permit or report text documents that conditional monitoring was not required for a period
No ordinary numeric measurement value is present in compiled reporting for the expectation
purpose_analytical: Documented no-discharge period as the established explanation for missing numeric result
Conditional monitoring not required as the established explanation
Other documented no-data state with a specific permitted or reported semantics
Required monitoring that appears to lack adequate evidence (gap) without inferring violation
Case remains unresolved when evidence does not support any established state

epistemic_requirements.grounding: Each established missing-evidence state must be grounded to permit provisions, DMR notations, or other source documentation—not inferred from absence alone
epistemic_requirements.no_missing_as_compliance_or_violation: Missing data by itself must not be interpreted as compliance or violation; only documented states or defensible evidence-backed classifications are permitted
epistemic_requirements.no_closed_world_negation: Do not assert that monitoring definitely did not occur unless a documented no-discharge, not-required, or equivalent no-data state is established
epistemic_requirements.world_vs_purpose_separation: World IR holds reported notations, permit no-discharge provisions, and schedule expectations; Purpose IR holds the classification of what a missing-result case establishes relative to Purpose C's analytical taxonomy

allowed_unresolved_states: Monitoring was likely expected but no numeric result and no documented no-discharge, not-required, or NODI explanation is available
NODI or missing notation is present but permit semantics for the code or context cannot be established
Conflicting documentation leaves the explanation for missing results indeterminate
Cannot determine whether a missing result reflects no discharge, waived monitoring, reporting omission, or analytical non-detect semantics
Linkage between a monitoring expectation and the absent result row cannot be reliably established

completeness_expectations.must_cover: FY2025 monitoring expectations at selected facilities that lack an ordinary numeric reported result and therefore fall outside Purpose A row evaluation
completeness_expectations.rows_when_resolved: Each row must identify the case and the evidence-established state among the purpose taxonomy (documented no-discharge, conditional not required, other documented no-data, or required-but-inadequate-evidence gap)
completeness_expectations.unresolved_when_not: Cases without sufficient evidence for any established state must appear in unresolved
completeness_expectations.receipt: Completeness should be receipted against the universe of in-scope missing-result expectations, cross-referenced with Purpose B obligation resolutions where relevant

purpose_specific_policies.missing_not_default_gap: Treat as inadequate-evidence gap only when monitoring requirement applicability is established (per Purpose B or equivalent grounding) and no documented no-data explanation applies
purpose_specific_policies.no_discharge_requires_documentation: Classify as documented no-discharge only when permit or reporting evidence explicitly supports no discharge for the period
purpose_specific_policies.not_required_requires_grounds: Classify as conditional monitoring not required only when condition evaluation and permit logic establish non-requirement for the period
purpose_specific_policies.separation_from_purpose_a: Do not perform numeric exceedance comparison in Purpose C; defer numeric limit evaluation to Purpose A when an ordinary numeric result exists
purpose_specific_policies.separation_from_purpose_b: Purpose C interprets missing results given obligations; Purpose B establishes whether monitoring was required—coordinate but do not collapse the distinctions
